root_cause.text: The sixpack_receive_buf() function failed to advance the data pointer (cp) when skipping bytes flagged with TTY errors, and subsequently passed the entire buffer (including error bytes) to sixpack_decode(), allowing uninitialized values from the TTY layer to be processed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows the old code had a while loop that decremented count but never incremented cp, and after the loop called `sixpack_decode(sp, cp, count1)` with the original `count1`, thus passing all bytes including error bytes. The new code increments `cp` inside the loop when skipping error bytes and only calls `sixpack_decode` for valid bytes one at a time, matching the pattern used by `slip_receive_buf()` and `mkiss_receive_buf()`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch shows the old code had a while loop that decremented count but never incremented cp, and after the loop called `sixpack_decode(sp, cp, count1)` with the original `count1`, thus passing all bytes including error bytes. The new code increments `cp` inside the loop when skipping error bytes and only calls `sixpack_decode` for valid bytes one at a time, matching the pattern used by `slip_receive_buf()` and `mkiss_receive_buf()`.

candidates.rationale: Part of function signature; receives cp and fp pointers; vulnerability stems from failing to advance cp.
Sets total byte count to include all bytes, including those with TTY errors, leading to error bytes being passed to decode.
Loop that iterates over buffer but does not advance cp; error bytes are not skipped.
Decrements count but does not advance cp, causing cp to stay at buffer start.
Checks for error flag and advances fp, but does not advance cp; this is where cp should be incremented for non-error bytes or skipped for errors.
Skips rest of loop on error without advancing cp; error bytes remain in buffer for decode.
Directly passes original cp (pointing to start) and full count1 to decode, causing all bytes including uninitialized error bytes to be processed.

vuln_statements.explanation: Loop iterates over buffer without advancing the data pointer cp, so all bytes (including those with TTY errors) remain in the buffer for subsequent processing.
Checks for TTY error flag and advances the flag pointer fp, but does not advance the data pointer cp, failing to skip the corresponding error byte in the data buffer.
Skips remaining loop body on error without advancing cp, leaving the error byte in the data buffer to be passed to sixpack_decode.
Decrements count but does not advance cp, so cp still points to the start of the buffer, causing all bytes (including error bytes) to be processed.
Passes the original cp (which has not been advanced past error bytes) and the full count1 (including error bytes) to decoding, causing uninitialized TTY error data to be processed.
Sets count1 to the total count including bytes with TTY errors, so that the later call to sixpack_decode processes the entire original buffer including uninitialized error bytes.
Part of function signature; fp and count are used in the loop, and the failure to advance cp relative to fp leads to processing of TTY error bytes.
